If our manufacturing equipment fails or if our equipment suppliers fail to perform under their contracts, we could experience production disruptions and be unable to satisfy our contractual requirements.” First Solar sources its laser tools from LPKF Laser & Electronics, which is headquartered and manufactures solar equipment in Germany. 3.4 Refined CdTe Powder This section focuses on the refined CdTe powder production step in the CdTe PV supply chain, including direct inputs. Here, refined CdTe powder includes CdSeTe or CdZnTe compositions used near the window layer or back surface fields in CdTe PV devices with arsenic or copper doping (Scarpulla et al. 2023). Figure 41 is a simplified supply chain diagram for refined CdTe powder production (Audet and Levitcharsky 2011; U.S. Geological Survey 2025e, 2025l, 2025n). Figure 41. Simplified supply chain diagram for refined CdTe powder production 3.4.1 Technology Trends for CdTe Powder The material composition of commercially available CdTe PV has evolved to include CdSeTe areas and CdZnTe in the absorber within approximately the past decade (Meagley et al. 2025). Use of ZnTe as the rear contact developed over this time as well. Typical material purities required for CdTe PV applications are around 5N–6N (Basore and Feldman 2022a). There are some examples of arsenic doping used in place of copper doping (Meagley et al. 2025). 3.4.2 Domestic Production of CdTe Powder We believe U.S. CdTe refining for PV does not occur at commercial scale. Most CdTe powder consumed in the United States is imported from Canada. Therefore, this section summarizes the domestic availability and production of its constituent materials. The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) estimated domestic production of primary refined cadmium at 0.3 kt in 2024, which could support more than 6 GW of CdTe PV production. The amount of dc secondary cadmium produced (recovered from nickel-cadmium battery recycling) is withheld, because only two producing facilities operated during 2024 (U.S. Geological Survey 2025e). 58 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications.
